evidence: src/domain/order-service.ts: `private reservations: Map<string, StockReservation[]> = new Map();` keeps reservations for all orders, keyed by orderId, across calls (a persistence/repository job)
src/domain/order-service.ts: `this.reservations.set(orderId, validItems);` in reserveStock saves records by id

src/domain/order-service.ts: releaseReservations and getReservedItems read records by id and delete them (`this.reservations.get(orderId)`, `this.reservations.delete(orderId)`), which are repository read and delete operations
Graph: CancelOrderUseCase, PlaceOrderUseCase and TransitionOrderUseCase all constructor-inject OrderDomainService, so this one instance's map acts as a shared store
Domain logic that belongs here: canTransition/validateTransition (state machine) and the all-or-nothing stock check in reserveStock
parsedVerdict.reasoning: Most of OrderDomainService is proper domain logic. canTransition and validateTransition enforce the order state machine. reserveStock checks every item against an injected checkStock predicate and fails as a whole if any item is short, throwing InsufficientStockError. The service also owns a private `reservations: Map<string, StockReservation[]>` keyed by orderId. That map lasts across calls and across orders. The application use cases and the server inject or import this one service instance, so the map works as the system's store of reservations. reservations.set, releaseReservations (get then delete), getReservedItems (get by id) and clearReservations are save, find-by-id and delete operations on that store. That is a repository or persistence job, which belongs in infrastructure behind a domain-defined port. A domain service should be stateless and should not keep records keyed by id. Confidence is moderate because the store is only in memory and is tied closely to the reservation rules. A lenient reading could treat it as domain state.

violations.message: OrderDomainService keeps a lasting reservation store (`reservations` Map keyed by orderId) and saves, reads and deletes records through reserveStock/releaseReservations/getReservedItems/clearReservations. This is a persistence/repository job that belongs in infrastructure behind a domain port, not in a stateless domain service.
